nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$. A sequence $p = (p_0, \dots, p_{n-1})$ of $n$ admissible steps of rank $r$ is a Motzkin path when its height after $k$ steps is nonnegative for every $k$ with $0 \le k \le n$ and its height after $n$ steps is $0$.
nodes.title: Colored Motzkin path condition

nodes.summary: For a sequence $p = (p_0, \dots, p_{n-1})$ of $n$ admissible steps of rank $r$ and a natural number $k$, the height of $p$ after $k$ steps is the integer $\sum_{i < \min(k, n)} h(p_i)$, where $h$ is the height change of a step. For $k \ge n$ it is the height of the whole sequence.
nodes.title: Height of a colored step sequence after k steps

nodes.summary: The height change of an admissible step of rank $r$ is the integer $j + 1$ for an up-step $U_j$ with $0 \le j < r$, $0$ for a level step, and $-(j + 1)$ for a down-step $D_j$ with $0 \le j < r$, whatever its color.
nodes.title: Height change of a colored Motzkin step

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $l$ be natural numbers and let $u, d \colon \{0, \dots, r - 1\} \to \mathbb{N}$. For every natural number $n$, the $(u,l,d)$-Motzkin number of rank $r$ and length $n$ equals the number of sequences of $n$ admissible steps of rank $r$ with these color counts that satisfy the Motzkin path condition.
nodes.title: The (u,l,d)-Motzkin number counts Motzkin step sequences

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $l$ be natural numbers and let $u, d \colon \{0, \dots, r - 1\} \to \mathbb{N}$. For a natural number $n$, the $(u,l,d)$-Motzkin number of rank $r$ and length $n$ is the number of colored Motzkin paths of rank $r$ and length $n$ whose up-steps $U_j$ come in $u(j)$ colors, whose level steps come in $l$ colors, and whose down-steps $D_j$ come in $d(j)$ colors.
nodes.title: (u,l,d)-Motzkin numbers of rank r

nodes.summary: For $r \ge 1$ and a natural number $n$, the colored Motzkin paths of rank $r$ and length $n$ are the sequences $(p_0, \dots, p_{n-1})$ of $n$ admissible steps of rank $r$ that satisfy the Motzkin path condition: the height after $k$ steps is nonnegative for every $k \le n$, and the height after $n$ steps is $0$.
nodes.title: Colored Motzkin paths of rank r and length n

nodes.summary: Let $r$ and $l$ be natural numbers and let $u, d \colon \{0, \dots, r - 1\} \to \mathbb{N}$. The admissible steps of rank $r$ are the up-steps $U_j$ with $0 \le j < r$ in one of $u(j)$ colors, the level steps in one of $l$ colors, and the down-steps $D_j$ with $0 \le j < r$ in one of $d(j)$ colors: the disjoint union of the sets $\{j\} \times \{0, \dots, u(j) - 1\}$ for $j < r$, the set $\{0, \dots, l - 1\}$, and…
nodes.title: Colored Motzkin steps of a given rank
